record.original_question: For which Fraisse classes with the strong amalgamation property (SAP) does the Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees? In particular, if such a class has finitely many relations and only finitely many forbidden substructures, or if all relations have arity at most two, must finite big Ramsey degrees always exist, and is there a general criterion characterizing exactly which SAP classes have this property?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. For which SAP Fraisse classes does the Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?

Subquestions are the following: Given an SAP Fraisse class with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, does its Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees? Results in [40] give evidence for a positive answer to this question. For such classes with relations of arity at most two, do big Ramsey degrees always exist? We would like a general condition on SAP classes characterizing those with finite big Ramsey degrees.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A relational language is a (here, finite or countable) set L of relation symbols, each with a fixed finite arity. An L-structure is a set together with an interpretation of each symbol of L. A class K of finite L-structures is a Fraïssé class if it is closed under isomorphism, contains structures of arbitrarily large finite cardinality, has only countably many isomorphism types, and satisfies:
 (HP) hereditary property: every substructure of a member of K is in K;
 (JEP) joint embedding property; and
 (AP) amalgamation property.
A Fraïssé class K has the strong amalgamation property (SAP) if whenever A, B, C ∈ K and f: A → B, g: A → C are embeddings, there exist D ∈ K and embeddings f′: B → D, g′: C → D with f′ ∘ f = g′ ∘ g and f′(B) ∩ g′(C) = f′(f(A)) = g′(g(A)). Every Fraïssé class K has a unique (up to isomorphism) countable homogeneous structure F = Flim(K) called its Fraïssé limit, characterized by being countable, locally K (every finitely generated substructure is in K), and ultrahomogeneous (every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism of F).

For a structure F and a finite substructure A ⊆ F, the big Ramsey degree T(A, F) is the least integer t ≥ 1 (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring of the set of copies of A in F, there is a substructure F′ ⊆ F isomorphic to F on which the copies of A take at most t colors. We say F has finite big Ramsey degrees if T(A, F) < ∞ for every finite substructure A of F.

A forbidden substructure description of a class is a specification of K = Forb(F) for some set F of finite L-structures, meaning K consists of all finite L-structures that admit no embedding from any member of F.

Problems.

(a) Characterize, in terms of intrinsic structural properties of K, exactly those Fraïssé classes K having the strong amalgamation property whose Fraïssé limit Flim(K) has finite big Ramsey degrees.

(b) Suppose K is an SAP Fraïssé class in a finite relational language defined by finitely many forbidden finite substructures, i.e., K = Forb(F) ∩ {finite L-structures} for some finite set F. Must Flim(K) have finite big Ramsey degrees?

(c) Suppose K is an SAP Fraïssé class in a relational language all of whose relation symbols have arity at most 2. Must Flim(K) have finite big Ramsey degrees?

artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization (part a) and the binary-arity case (part c) appear to remain open. Significant progress on part (b) was made by Balko–Chodounský–Dobrinen–Hubička–Konečný–Vena–Zucker and by Zucker, who proved that for finite binary relational languages with finitely many forbidden irreducible substructures, the corresponding free-amalgamation Fraïssé limit has finite big Ramsey degrees, with exact values computed in subsequent work. A full characterization for arbitrary SAP classes is still sought as an active open problem in current surveys.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys current open problems on which Fraïssé limits have finite big Ramsey degrees, including SAP classes.
status_evidence.claim: The general characterization for SAP Fraïssé classes remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Exact big Ramsey degrees for finitely constrained binary free amalgamation classes
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes exact big Ramsey degrees for free amalgamation classes in finite binary languages with finitely many forbidden irreducible substructures.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results exist for the finitely-constrained binary free amalgamation case.
